deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from p.176). Gauss sets up the ellipse with semi-axes a, b. He writes T = x+iy and T' = x-iy. He seeks T as an odd power series T = t + A t^3 + B t^5 + ... in an auxiliary variable t = cos(phi)+i sin(phi), with T' = t^-1 + A t^-3 + ... . So t -> T is an analytic, symmetric map of the unit disk whose boundary circle goes onto the ellipse. In modern terms this is the CONFORMAL MAP OF THE DISK ONTO THE INTERIOR OF AN ELLIPSE, normalised to T'(0)=1.

The ellipse equation x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 rewritten in T, T' is
  k(T^2 + T'^2) = TT' - 2a^2b^2/(a^2+b^2), with k = (a^2-b^2)/(2(a^2+b^2)).
I checked this. Requiring every non-constant Laurent coefficient of TT' - k(TT+T'T') to vanish fixes A, B, ... as power series in k. Page 176 tabulates them.

PAGE 177, step by step.

(1) Closed forms for the 'vertical columns' of the k-table, i.e. the leading, second and third terms in each row, as generating functions in t.
- Column 1: sum_n C_n k^n t^(2n+1) = (1 - sqrt(1-4kt^2))/(2kt). These are the Catalan numbers 1, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, 429.
- Column 2: [1 - (1-2kt^2-2k^2t^4)(1-4kt^2)^(-1/2)]/(2t^3) = -2k^3t^3 - 9k^4t^5 - 36k^5t^7 - 140k^6t^9 - 540k^7t^11 - 2079k^8t^13 - 8008k^9t^15 - ... . This matches p.176 exactly. The sign of the k^2 t^4 term must be minus (see transcription corrections).
- Column 3: (k/t^5){1 - kt^2 - (1-7kt^2+12k^2t^4-2k^3t^6-k^4t^8)(1-4kt^2)^(-3/2)} = 3k^5t^3 + 24k^6t^5 + 142k^7t^7 + 740k^8t^9 + 3600k^9t^11 + 16786k^10t^13 + ... . The k^4 t term cancels. This confirms the doubtful '16786' of p.176.

(2) The constant term of TT' (on |t|=1, the sum of squares of the coefficients) is
  N(k) = 1 + k^2 + 0k^4 - k^6 - k^8 + k^10 ... = 1/(1 - k^2 + k^4 + 0 + 0 - k^10 ...).
This fixes the scale: the true map is c*T with c^2 N = 2a^2b^2/(a^2+b^2).

(3) Change of parameter to lambda = (a-b)/(a+b). Then k = lambda/(1+lambda^2), and conversely
  lambda = k + k^3 + 2k^5 + 5k^7 + 14k^9 + 42k^11 + ... = (1 - sqrt(1-4k^2))/(2k) (Catalan inversion).
Re-expanding the p.176 table in lambda gives the new table T = t + t^3(lambda - 3lambda^3 + 10lambda^5 - 29lambda^7 + 73lambda^9 ...) + ... . The same table reappears in columns on p.178.

(4) Comparison with the eccentric-anomaly parametrisation. Put u = e^{iE}, so the true point is a cos E + i b sin E = ((a+b)/2)(u + lambda u^-1). Gauss states
  T(normalised) = G * (u + lambda u^-1), with G = 1 + 2lambda^2 + lambda^4 + 2lambda^6 + 2lambda^8 + 0*lambda^10 + ... .
The asterisk marks the vanishing lambda^10 term. My check: G^2 = (1+lambda^2)N/(1-lambda^2)^2 = 1 + 4q + 6q^2 + 8q^3 + 13q^4 + ..., where q = lambda^2. Hence the true map is f(t) = ((a+b)/(2G)) T_norm(t), with f'(0) = (a+b)/(2G).
My identification: G = (sum_{n>=0} q^{n(n+1)/2})^2 = psi(q)^2 = theta_2(q) theta_3(q)/(2q^{1/4}), with q = lambda^2. Here psi is the generating function of triangular numbers, and the q^5 coefficient is indeed 0.

(5) Boundary correspondence between the conformal angle phi (t = e^{i phi}) and the eccentric anomaly E (u = e^{iE}).
- t = u + lambda(u^-1 - u^3) + lambda^2(-u + u^5) + lambda^3(-u^-1 + 2u^3 - u^7) + lambda^4(-u^-3 + 2u - 2u^5 + u^9) + ...
- log t = log u + lambda(u^-2 - u^2) + lambda^2(-u^-4/2 + u^4/2) + lambda^3(u^-6/3 - u^-2 + u^2 - u^6/3) + lambda^4(-u^-8/4 + u^8/4) + ...
  In real form: phi = E - 2lambda sin2E + lambda^2 sin4E + lambda^3(2 sin2E - (2/3) sin6E) + (1/2)lambda^4 sin8E + ... .
  The pattern (my inference, consistent with every printed term) is log t = log u + sum_n ((-1)^(n+1)/n) lambda^n/(1+lambda^(2n)) (u^(-2n) - u^(2n)).
  Equivalently, t = u * prod_{m>=0} [(1+lambda^(2m+1)u^-2)/(1+lambda^(2m+1)u^2)]^((-1)^m).
  This is a Jacobi-type q-expansion with nome q = lambda^2, matching Schwarz's elliptic-function map, whose nome is ((a-b)/(a+b))^2.
- Inverse series:
  u = t + lambda(t^3 - t^-1) + lambda^2(2t^5 - t - t^-3) + lambda^3(5t^7 - 4t^3 + t^-1 - 2t^-5) + lambda^4(14t^9 - 15t^5 + 2t + 4t^-3 - 5t^-7) + ...
  log u = log t + lambda(t^2 - t^-2) + (3/2)lambda^2(t^4 - t^-4) + lambda^3((10/3)t^6 - 2t^2 + 2t^-2 - (10/3)t^-6) + lambda^4((35/4)t^8 - 8t^4 + 8t^-4 - (35/4)t^-8).
  The leading coefficients binom(2n-1,n)/n are those of log of the Catalan generating function.

'Gesetz gefunden 1839 Oct. 9, siehe S. 222': Gauss records that he found the law of these coefficients, presumably the 1/(1+lambda^(2n)) structure and the q-series G.
errors: No mathematical errors found in any coefficient I could check. I verified: columns 1-3 of the k-table; the constant term of TT' and its reciprocal; lambda(k); every lambda-table entry through t^15 except 73, 1007 and -11665, which need k-coefficients absent from p.176; 36190 (confirmed); G through lambda^8; and the mutual consistency of the four t/u/log series through lambda^4.

The truncation dots '+', '-' at row ends are just continuation signs. The 'constant part' and G are given only to finite order without proof, so the law is inductive (empirical), not derived on the page.

results.what: Power-series construction of the conformal map of the unit disk onto the interior of an ellipse, via the functional equation k(T^2+T'^2) = TT' - const and the boundary condition T' = conj(T) on |t|=1
results.modern_name: Conformal map of disk onto ellipse interior (Schwarz's elliptic-sn map)
results.usually_credited_to: H. A. Schwarz (1869); series methods later (Szegő polynomials, Kantorovich-Krylov)

results.what: Generating functions of the first three 'columns' of the coefficient table: Catalan GF and corrections with (1-4kt^2)^(-1/2), (1-4kt^2)^(-3/2)
results.modern_name: Catalan generating function and central-binomial generating functions

results.what: Reparametrisation by lambda = (a-b)/(a+b), with k = lambda/(1+lambda^2) and lambda = (1-sqrt(1-4k^2))/(2k)
results.usually_credited_to: standard (Landen, Gauss AGM circle of ideas)

results.what: Normalising factor G = 1+2q+q^2+2q^3+2q^4+0q^5..., q = lambda^2, relating the normalised conformal map to the eccentric-anomaly parametrisation; equals psi(q)^2 = theta_2 theta_3/(2q^(1/4)), giving conformal radius (a+b)/(2 psi(lambda^2)^2)
results.modern_name: Theta-function formula for the conformal radius of an ellipse
results.usually_credited_to: follows from Schwarz 1869 with Jacobi theta functions

results.what: Boundary correspondence: phi = E + 2 sum (-1)^n lambda^n/(n(1+lambda^(2n))) sin 2nE, i.e. log t = log u + sum ((-1)^(n+1)/n) lambda^n/(1+lambda^(2n)) (u^-2n - u^2n), and its inverse
results.modern_name: Fourier/q-expansion of the boundary correspondence function of the ellipse (Jacobi-type amplitude series with nome lambda^2)
results.usually_credited_to: Schwarz (1869) / Jacobi-type expansions; not usually attributed to anyone before Schwarz

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's 1822 conformal-mapping work is famous, but the explicit disk-to-ellipse-interior map is classically attributed to Schwarz (1869). Here, in 1839, Gauss computes it by series and finds the q-structure with nome lambda^2: the factor psi(lambda^2)^2 and the lambda^n/(1+lambda^2n) law of the boundary correspondence. Given his known elliptic/theta mastery, this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a revolution. The 'law' is stated empirically, and its proof or full form is on p.222.

transcription_corrections: Second column: the factor is (1-2ktt-2kkt^4), not (1-2ktt+2kktt^4). The sign is minus and the power is t^4. Only the minus sign reproduces -2k^3t^3-9k^4t^5-... of p.176.
t^13 row lambda^10 coefficient is 36190 (confirmed by computation and by p.178), not uncertain.
In the G series '1+2λλ+λ^4+2λ^6+2λ^8 *', the asterisk marks a zero coefficient of λ^10, consistent with psi(q)^2.
